title: Question every requirement
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which rule are you following only because someone smart told you to?
I went through the five points from the book. I read the first.
You should never accept the requirement from the legal department or the safety department.

You need to know the real name of the person who made the requirement, I said, and you should question it no matter how smart the person is. Sometimes the requirements from the smart people are the most dangerous, because people ask fewer questions.
I said the second is: delete any process you don't need. What process in your day would you eliminate?
A student said: I meet every day with a freelancer, and sometimes we aren't efficient. We look at things together that she could do on her own. That would be a more efficient use of my time.
I said: that is great. I also said the third was to accelerate the cycle time and automate.
What would you delete this week?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one requirement you follow without knowing who set it.
Write the person's real name, or find it.
Write one process you would delete.
Write one meeting you could shorten.
Write one thing you could automate.

check.q: What did I say you need to know about a requirement?
choices: The real name of the person who made it

check.q: Why can requirements from smart people be dangerous?
What is the second point I read?
choices: Delete any process you don't need

recap: Know who set the rule. Delete processes you don't need.
